blogs.title: How Bee implemented Zero Operator Access for personal AI on AWS
blogs.summary: Bee, an Amazon company, built a personal AI wearable with no mechanism for operators (Bee engineers, other Amazon employees, or AWS infrastructure operators) to access customer data. Learn how Bee uses Amazon EC2 instance attestation and the AWS Nitro System to achieve Zero Operator Access (ZOA).

blogs.title: AI coding agents on Amazon EC2 Mac: How Cognition scales Devin for macOS
blogs.summary: Cognition gave its AI software engineer, Devin, a cloud Mac. Each Devin session gets a fresh macOS VM on Amazon EC2 Mac bare metal hosts, so Devin can build, run, and test iOS and macOS apps. Learn how Cognition built it with disk snapshots, a user-space network gateway, prepared guest images, and accessibility-based control.

blogs.title: How Country Road Group built a pattern-driven integration solution on AWS
blogs.summary: Country Road Group replaced Microsoft BizTalk with a pattern-driven, serverless integration platform on AWS. Learn how its Strategic Integration Platform works across four processing lanes, and get the open-source Enterprise Integration Patterns CDK library to apply the same approach to your own middleware.

blogs.title: Aderant modernizes analytics data pipeline with Apache Iceberg and AWS Lambda
blogs.summary: Learn how Aderant modernized the data pipeline behind its Stridyn legal analytics platform with Apache Iceberg, AWS Lambda, and AWS Glue, moving from 15-minute batch cycles to an event-driven medallion architecture that processes change data capture events in single-digit seconds for 700 tenants, with 10-26x faster queries and 77 percent lower cost.

blogs.title: How United Airlines streams database changes to Apache Iceberg with Amazon Data Firehose
blogs.summary: United Airlines built a near-real-time change data capture pipeline that replicates reference data from Amazon Aurora MySQL to open Apache Iceberg tables using AWS DMS, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, and Amazon Data Firehose. This post shows how to reproduce the serverless, multi-engine analytics pattern with AWS CloudFormation.

blogs.title: Resilience testing your agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
blogs.summary: When an AI agent's tools fail or return corrupted data, does it fail safe or confidently fabricate an answer? Learn how to inject tool-level faults (cancelled calls, corrupted responses, stripped fields) into a Strands agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using AWS Fault Injection Service, and build the observability to tell a safe failure from a silent one.

blogs.title: Block DNS threats with Infoblox rules in Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall
blogs.summary: Infoblox Threat Defense is now available in preview in Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall, providing partner-managed DNS threat intelligence. Learn how to add an Infoblox managed rule to a rule group, test it in alert mode, monitor matches, and move to blocking.

blogs.title: How Rakbank built centralized observability at scale with Amazon OpenSearch Service
blogs.summary: Rakbank re-platformed logging for its retail digital banking workloads on a cross-account, Multi-AZ Amazon OpenSearch Service design that ingests ~150 GB/day through Fluent Bit, using hot/UltraWarm/cold tiering and Amazon S3 archival for 7-year compliance retention and ~55% cost savings over an all-hot cluster.

blogs.title: Announcing updates to the AWS Well-Architected Framework
blogs.summary: Updates to the AWS Well-Architected Framework reorganize it into Well-Architected Cloud Foundations and Well-Architected Cloud Workloads, add new best practices, and bring the general availability of the AWS Well-Architected Agent for analyzing workloads and guiding remediation.

blogs.title: Engineering AI Discover
Probing DNS at Cloudflare
blogs.summary: At Cloudflare we’ve built tools to enable teams to extend our internal testing framework and build test tooling for networking protocols. This is the story of how this was used for DNS.

blogs.title: How Cloudflare WAF protects against ruby2shell (CVE-2026-132825)
blogs.summary: ruby2shell lets attackers corrupt memory in default Rails and Sinatra apps without logging in. Cloudflare WAF blocks it for every customer, including Free plans. Upgrade Ruby now, and use the WAF to cover the gap.

blogs.title: How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against phpAfterShell and other critical PHP flaws
blogs.summary: phpAfterShell is a critical flaw in PHP's default session handler that can lead to code execution. Cloudflare WAF blocks it for all customers, including Free plans, and adds new rules for other PHP flaws fixed in the same release.

blogs.title: nginx2root: Five new nginx vulnerabilities, and how Cloudflare protects origins from the worst of them
blogs.summary: Five memory corruption bugs in nginx, called nginx2root, can let an unauthenticated attacker run code on a server. Here’s how they work, and why origins behind Cloudflare's proxy are shielded from the most serious of these bugs.
